intro: On September 1, 2030, UFV receives an operational autonomous-aviation ecosystem — not merely infrastructure.
incomplete: A finished building without field sites is incomplete;
field sites without technology/data systems are incomplete;
technology without trained people is incomplete;
and equipment without academic/research pathways does not make UFV meaningfully better.

items.name: Innovation & Simulation Node
items.receives: Commissioned central capability for simulation, mission planning, prototyping, secure compute/data, research, teaching, and partner collaboration.

items.name: Fraser Valley Field-Test Network
items.receives: At least three proposed-target compliant field environments representing different operating needs; exact sites determined through feasibility.

items.name: Modular Autonomous-Aircraft Fleet
items.receives: Controlled portfolio selected from validated missions and regulatory requirements; no invented aircraft count.

items.name: Sensor & Payload Library
items.receives: Flexible optical, mapping, multispectral, thermal, environmental, positioning/navigation, and research payload capability as justified.

items.name: Simulation / Mission-Control / Data Platform
items.receives: Integrated pre-flight simulation/planning, authorized operational monitoring, secure data transfer, storage, processing, analytics, and visualization.

items.name: Safety & Regulatory Operating System
items.receives: Operating categories, qualifications, SMS, SOPs, maintenance, incident/emergency procedures, authorization and insurance/liability processes.

items.name: Cybersecurity, Privacy & Data Governance
items.receives: System access, network/C2 security, firmware/software management, partner/research data rules, imagery/personal-data controls, retention/sharing/deletion, incident response.

items.name: Student Applied-Learning Program
items.receives: Formal routes through courses, capstones, co-op/practica, research assistantships, multidisciplinary challenges and partner projects.

items.name: Applied Research Program
items.receives: Clear route from concept → simulation → prototype → approved field test → analysis → research/partner output.

items.name: Industry & Community Challenge Program
items.receives: Defined intake process beginning with partner problem, not “we have a drone — what can we sell you?”

items.name: Strategic Partnership Portfolio
items.receives: Proposed launch target ≥8 substantive written external agreements across more than one sector/type.

items.name: Trained Operating Organization
items.receives: All necessary operational/safety/technical/academic/partner functions staffed or assigned before launch; exact headcount determined from workload.

items.name: Sustainable Operating Model
items.receives: Five-year operating plan, staffing/maintenance, technology refresh, funding mix, lifecycle plan, governance and benefits review.

items.name: Tested Integrated Capability
items.receives: Representative end-to-end missions prove people, technology, field sites, safety, data and partner/student workflows operate as a coherent system.

loop: Lessons fed into the next challenge
definitionOfDone: SkyGrid is not “done” when construction ends, when drones arrive, or when a website launches. SkyGrid is done when UFV can safely take a real partner or research problem, involve students and faculty, design and simulate an autonomous-aviation approach, obtain the required operating authorization, test it in an appropriate Fraser Valley environment, securely analyze the resulting data, and deliver a meaningful educational, research, or partner outcome within a sustainable operating model.
